questions.q: What does the German word Bildung mean in bildungsroman?
choices: Building, as in a house or a plot
Picture, as in a portrait of an era
Formation or cultivation: the shaping of a whole person
Journey or road
questions.explain: A bildungsroman is a novel of formation: a young person's character and place in the world, shaped over time.

questions.q: A film ends with its young hero accepting a job in his hometown and getting engaged, at peace with the life on offer. Which classic ending is this?
choices: Rupture
Accommodation
Catastrophe
Dénouement by deus ex machina
questions.explain: Accommodation: the young person makes peace with society and takes a place in it, as Wilhelm Meister does.

questions.q: A novel follows a young painter who breaks with her family and religion and ends by leaving her country to make art. What's the term for this branch of the form?
choices: Picaresque
Künstlerroman
Roman à clef
Well-made play
questions.explain: The künstlerroman, or artist novel, follows an artist's growth and usually ends in a break, as in Joyce's Portrait of the Artist.

questions.q: In Great Expectations, what does Pip's education finally consist of?
choices: Learning a trade and taking over the forge
Learning that his expectations, and his snobbery, were wrong
Learning to write, so that he becomes a novelist
Learning the secret society that guided him all along
questions.explain: Pip discovers his benefactor is the convict he helped, and that the people he looked down on were the ones worth having.

questions.q: A critic says a novel about a girl in 1800 can't follow the classic pattern because she can't leave home, choose a career or roam. Which argument is she making?
choices: The critique from The Voyage In: women's development often takes delayed, inward or blocked shapes
Aristotle's view that episodic plots are the worst
Moretti's claim that the form is mainly about money
Vonnegut's point that some stories are flat lines
questions.explain: Abel, Hirsch and Langland argued the classic form assumed a young man's freedoms, so female development often ends elsewhere: marriage, madness or death.

questions.q: You're writing a stage coming-of-age story and can't show years of growth in two hours. What does the lesson suggest?
choices: Narrate each year in a voice-over
Cast several actors as the same character at different ages, scene by scene
Compress the formation into one season or crisis where change happens fastest
Avoid the form on stage altogether
questions.explain: Theatre usually compresses formation into a crisis, as Spring Awakening does with one season of adolescence.

questions.q: Moonlight tells its hero's life in three chapters titled Little, Chiron and Black. What does that structure do for a bildungsroman?
choices: It marks each stage of formation by the name he's given or takes, so identity itself is what's being formed
It turns the film into a picaresque with no development
It creates a Man in a Hole shape
It reveals the identity of a secret benefactor
questions.explain: Each chapter's name shows who he is at that age, so the question 'who will he be?' is built into the structure.

ideas: Which approach promises we'll watch a young person become someone, educated by mistakes, mentors, love and work?
Which approach ends either in accommodation, taking a place in society, or in rupture, refusing it?
Which approach took its model from Goethe's Wilhelm Meister, guided in secret by the Society of the Tower?
Which approach has an artist's branch, ending with the young artist breaking away from home to make art?
